📌 Prediction Markets: Trading on Future Events

Main Points
⏺ Prediction markets let you trade on the outcome of events like elections, sports, or crypto decisions
⏺ Prices act like probabilities, showing what the crowd “thinks” will happen
⏺ This post explains how prediction markets turn opinions into tradable assets

1️⃣ Core Idea — instead of just guessing who will win, you buy “Yes” or “No” shares tied to a specific outcome
2️⃣ Pricing — if a “Yes” share trades at $0.70, the market is roughly saying there’s a 70% chance of that result
3️⃣ Settlement — after the event, winning shares pay out $1 while losing ones go to zero
4️⃣ Use Cases — forecasting politics, economic data, protocol decisions, and even on-chain governance outcomes
5️⃣ Signal Power — because people risk real money, prediction markets can sometimes be more accurate than polls or surveys

Final Thoughts

Prediction markets turn beliefs into positions — the stronger your conviction, the more you’re willing to back it with real capital.

Spain exempts self-custody wallets from crypto tax reporting

Spain's tax authorities have confirmed that cryptocurrency held in self-custody wallets — where the owner controls the private keys — does not need to be reported under Form 721, the country's disclosure form for foreign-held digital assets. The exemption hinges on one condition: no third party holds the assets on your behalf.

The rule draws a clean line between personal custody and exchange or custodial holdings abroad, which remain reportable. Simple in principle, potentially significant in practice — Spain just gave self-custody a regulatory edge.

📌 Why is Stacks (STX) going up? 

📣 Stacks has gained more than 100% over the past 90 days, backed by institutional Bitcoin Staking that is creating a new use for STX that could grow as more BTC enters future bonding periods. According to CoinGecko data, STX was trading around $0.38 on Oct. 6 after gaining roughly 18% over the previous week. The token had already climbed 108% in the 90 days through Sept. 27.

🌐 Those developments have given traders several Stacks specific catalysts at a time when many major altcoins have struggled to match STX’s gains. Bitcoin Staking is particularly important to the long term case because it gives institutions a way to earn BTC rewards while creating a separate use for STX. However, Bitcoin Staking alone cannot account for the entire 90 day rally on its own. Market conditions and renewed interest in the Stacks ecosystem have contributed to the price action as well. But unlike a short term price catalyst, the staking model creates a measurable link between institutional BTC participation and the amount of STX needed to support it.

➡️ The Genesis Bond has already put that relationship into practice, while Bond 2 and subsequent bonding periods will test whether it can repeat as more Bitcoin enters the program. Bitcoin Staking on Stacks allows BTC holders to earn BTC denominated rewards without changing Bitcoin’s proof of work consensus. Under Stacks’ Proof of Transfer system, miners commit BTC to compete for Stacks blocks and receive STX. The BTC committed through the process becomes the source of rewards distributed through the staking system.

She Survived a Botched Execution. Now Christa Pike Is Awake and Speaking #️⃣


Christa Pike, the Tennessee death-row inmate whose execution failed last week, is conscious and able to speak, according to her attorneys. The development comes days after officials attempted to put her to death by lethal injection in a case that has raised new questions about the state’s execution procedures.

Pike, 50, was scheduled to be executed on September 30 at the Tennessee prison where she has been held for decades. The procedure did not go as planned. After receiving two doses of pentobarbital, she reportedly remained alive and was eventually placed on a ventilator.

Her attorneys now say Pike has regained consciousness and is communicating. They describe her condition as serious, however, and say she faces a prolonged recovery.

According to the legal team, Pike suffered significant injuries to her hands during the failed execution, including burns, swelling and blistering. Her lawyers have requested access to medical records and other documentation that could help establish exactly what happened inside the execution chamber.

The case has quickly become a major issue for Tennessee officials. Gov. Bill Lee ordered an independent review of the execution and paused subsequent executions in the state while the circumstances are investigated.

Pike’s lawyers are also seeking to have her death sentence changed to life in prison without the possibility of parole. They argue that the failed execution and the injuries she sustained raise serious constitutional and legal questions about whether the state should be permitted to attempt another execution.

Pike was convicted in the 1995 killing of Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old woman who was a fellow student at a Tennessee technical college. Prosecutors said Pike and two accomplices lured Slemmer into a wooded area, where she was attacked and killed.

The case attracted national attention because of the brutality of the crime and Pike’s age at the time. She was 18 when Slemmer was murdered, making her one of the youngest women ever sentenced to death in the United States.

Pike has spent decades on death row while her case moved through the courts. Her execution had already been delayed several times, including because of questions surrounding the state’s lethal-injection procedures.
The latest failure has placed those procedures under renewed scrutiny.

The central question now is what happened during the execution attempt and why the state was unable to carry it out. Medical and legal records are expected to play a key role in determining whether the problems were caused by the equipment, the injection process, Pike’s medical condition or a combination of factors.

For now, Pike remains alive and under medical care.
Her attorneys say the fact that she is conscious and speaking represents a significant change from the days immediately following the failed execution.

But they caution that her recovery could be lengthy and that the full extent of her injuries remains unclear.
The state’s investigation could ultimately determine whether Tennessee attempts to carry out Pike’s sentence again—or whether the extraordinary circumstances surrounding the failed execution lead to a different legal outcome.

What was supposed to be the final hours of a death-row inmate’s life has instead opened a new chapter in a case that has already lasted more than three decades.
